archive.title: This design software reimagines everyday objects as self-aware devices
archive.summary: MIT researchers developed X-Hinges, software that helps design 3D-printed objects with built-in sensors. The tricky part is separating the sensors’ signals from interference caused by the wire-like connections around them. The tool places two different materials in the design to reduce that interference. The researchers describe objects such as lamps and gloves that respond to touch, as well as small robots and toys. It is an understandable electronics problem: make an object sense what someone is doing, then get a clear signal out of it.

But scientists at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) are now doing something similar: transforming stationary items into self-aware tools that perceive and respond to human motion to complete a task. Engineers have 3D-printed these dynamic items with built-in sensing, using conductive materials for sensors and traces (sort of like wires) inside. archive.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Trump's express wish to take over the East Potomac Golf Links has thrust a municipal D.C. golf course into the national spotlight. The southern tip of East Potomac Park, known as Hains Point, is beloved by cyclists, runners, picnickers and birders for its waterfront views, cherry trees and Ohio Drive, the scenic three-mile loop around its perimeter. Runners use the wide, flat road to train; it's even a fixture of several major race courses, including the Marine Corps Marathon on Sunday.

archive.summary: Mink farming will end in Denmark by August 2029 after the government decided to drop plans to pursue an exemption to an EU-wide ban on the practice. Danish Nature Minister Christian Rabjerg Madsen said the government had chosen animal welfare.
